narrative.markdown:
**At a glance** — emerging: currently **Emerging** (confidence 95%); over the next 12 months the level is expected to change by **+45.4%** (upward). Probability of increase 96%, forecast confidence high.

## Past: how it got here
- Analysed 120 monthly observations from Jan 2016 to Dec 2025 (about 10 years).
- On the trend line the level moved from 4.67 to 68.4, a total change of **+1,364.8%** (**+31.1%** per year, CAGR).
- The Mann-Kendall test finds a statistically significant **upward** trend (τ = 0.69, p < 0.001 after correcting for autocorrelation). The long-run slope is +0.18/mo (+1.30%/mo of the mean level).
- The peak was 69.9 in Dec 2025 — the series is at (or right next to) its all-time high now.
- 3 structural breaks detected:
  - From **Apr 2022**: growth accelerating (slope 0.019 → 0.46/mo, strength 0.49)
  - From **Oct 2023**: growth accelerating (slope 0.46 → 1.51/mo, strength 0.91)
  - From **Dec 2024**: growth accelerating (slope 1.51 → 2.28/mo, strength 0.62)
- 12 months of data have accumulated since the latest break (Dec 2024).
- No statistical anomalies were detected.
- Seasonality is negligible (strength 0.04); trend consistency is very high (trend strength 0.99).

## Present: where it stands now
- Current lifecycle phase: **Emerging** (confidence 95%).
- Evidence: The trend level is 14.6× its earlier base: fast growth from a low base.
- Evidence: Over the last 18 months the trend changed by +144.2%.
- Evidence: The recent rise is 4.2× the average pace of the whole period (trend start to end): accelerating.
- Evidence: A structural break (growth accelerating) was detected in Dec 2024.
- Over the last 12 months the trend changed by **+68.5%**.
- Momentum (recent minus long-run slope, relative to the current trend level) is +3.91 pp/mo: growing faster than its long-run pace (accelerating).
- Volatility (residual coefficient of variation) is 8.5% — moderate.
- Latest value: 69.9 (Dec 2025); average over the last 12 months: 56.1.

## Outlook
- The average forecast over the next 12 months is expected to change by **+45.4%** from the average of the last 12 months (**upward**; forecast to Dec 2026).
- Probability that the average forecast over the next 12 months is higher than the average of the last 12 months: about **96%** — a rise is very likely.
- Scenarios for Dec 2026 (80% interval; % vs. the latest value (Dec 2025), 69.9): pessimistic 72.1 (+3.1%) · base 91.2 (+30.4%) · optimistic 110.2 (+57.6%); 95% interval 59.1 – 123.2. These are single end-point values, so they can differ from the average-based change and probability above.
- No distinct forecast peak (rise, then fall) within the horizon.
- Projected phase shift: **Emerging** → **Growing**.
- Forecast confidence: **high**.
- Accuracy: in backtests on past data the error was **about 64%** lower than that of the best simple benchmark (repeat the last value, repeat the last season, or extend the straight line). (Technical note: backtest MASE 1.34, which scales the errors by the in-sample one-step seasonal-naive error; multi-step forecasts often score above 1 even when they beat naive.)
- Method: a single model, logistic S-curve — the most accurate of the backtested candidates. (model ids: logistic_growth)

caveats.markdown:
- Uncertainty grows with the horizon: the 80% interval widens from ±4.91 at the first step to ±19.1 at the last (about 3.9×). Judge by the range, not a single number.
- Just as the past contains 3 structural breaks, an external shock (market, policy, technology) can change the trend abruptly — the model cannot foresee that.
- Only 12 observations follow the latest break (Dec 2024), so whether the new regime lasts is not yet well tested.
- This is a statistical extrapolation of past patterns, not a guarantee — and not financial or investment advice.
caveats.disclaimer: Forecasts assume past patterns continue. Sudden events and outside factors (prices, ads, holidays) are not included.
